articles.title: Your First 90 Days as an Adult Beginner
articles.excerpt: What to expect in month 1–3 when starting from scratch.
content: You do not have to start piano as a child to play well. Adult beginners progress quickly because they know what music inspires them.
In month one, we focus on comfort and simple two-hand patterns. By month three, most adults can sit down and play full songs they love with 15 minutes of daily practice.

articles.title: How Piano Helps Kids Focus & Shine
articles.excerpt: Why music builds patience, memory, and self-confidence.
content: Coordinating both hands while listening closely strengthens focus, memory, and creative confidence.
Finishing a song and playing it for family shows kids that steady, playful practice pays off.

articles.title: The 15-Minute Smart Practice Routine
articles.excerpt: Short focused sessions beat long distracted practice.
content: Split 15 minutes into: 3 minutes warm-up, 8 minutes looping only the tricky 2 bars slowly, and 4 minutes playing through for fun.
Slow, accurate practice helps your hands learn twice as fast.

faqs.question: Do I need a piano at home before starting?
faqs.answer: No! Come for your first lesson first — we'll help you pick an affordable keyboard or digital piano in Uganda when you're ready.

faqs.question: Where in Entebbe are lessons held?
faqs.answer: In-person in Entebbe, Monday through Saturday. Message on WhatsApp for directions or nearby home-visit slots.

faqs.question: Can total beginners (kids or adults) join?
faqs.answer: Yes! Most of our students start with zero musical background — we teach everything step by step.

faqs.question: What styles can I learn?
faqs.answer: Pop, gospel & worship, classical, film themes, or playing by ear — tailored to what excites you.
